$comment: NIP-FP conformance fixtures. Each case lists UNSIGNED event templates, in dependency order, with the fixture key that signs each. Placeholders: {pk:<key>} is that key's hex pubkey; {id:<ref>} is the id of an earlier event once signed. `auth` adds a NIP-OA tag from the named owner with empty conditions. `mutate` corrupts the copy the origin serves (tamper_sig flips the signature; tamper_content changes content under the original id). `served_except` lists events the origin withholds from the viewer. The fingerprint is signed last, selecting the named refs at `origin`. `expect.items` is exhaustive and flattens the report: `rung` and `viewer_known` come from the interpretation, every other field from the observed item. Every event the verifier reports must appear, keyed by ref, and nothing else; listed fields must match. `rung: null` means no rung. Signing is not deterministic across implementations, so consumers sign with these keys and compare by ref. Spec: docs/nips/NIP-FP.md.

cases.name: control_merged_pr
cases.note: Passing control. The subject's PR is merged by the repo owner, and a relay-signed ref state shows main at the merge commit. The merger is unrelated by any owner link, so independence is unknown, never independent. The viewer's policy knows the maintainer, so the rung-2 basis is viewer_known.

cases.note: A PR with no status at all. It is attributed (rung 1) and the interpretation reports that no outcome was found in scope before the cutoff, not that the PR failed.

cases.name: self_endorsement
cases.note: A sibling agent of the subject's owner asks, the subject answers, and the sibling accepts. The acceptance is authorized (the sibling is the requester) but same_owner, so it never raises the rung. The subject's own label is an opinion from the same signer.

template.content: How should the uploader retry after a 503?

cases.name: sybil_ring
cases.note: Two fresh keys with no owner links ask, accept, and praise the subject's answer. Signatures cannot tell them from strangers: the acceptance is authorized and reaches rung 2, but with independence unknown and not viewer_known. Only viewer policy can discount it; the report never calls it independent.
